newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: NSW POLICE IN PAY ROW
New South Wales police are threatening industrial action in support of a 25 per cent wage claim.
The Police Association delivered the demand in a meeting with Minister Paul Whelan today.
Mr Whelan came into the meeting ready to offer police a three percent rise and another review next year.
The Police Association's Lloyd Taylor says police will begin industrial, legal and political action if the 25 per cent demand isn't met.
Mr Whelan called the 25 per cent rise an ambit claim, saying one month ago the Association was looking for five percent, and he's vowed not to cave in.
BOX MAKERS ANGERED BY WOOLIES BAN
Polystyrene box manufacturers say a ban by Woolworths on the use of the boxes for fresh produce, could have a devastating effect on the industry.
The Association of Extended Polystyrene Manufacturers, says the supermarket chain will not accept broccoli, stone fruit, tomatoes and grapes in the boxes because of difficulties with disposal.
Association Chairman, Robert Zahara, says Woolworths has refused to accept an industry offer to collect the boxes for recycling.
Woolworths was not available for a response
PM'S STANCE ON GAY MARDI GRAS APPLAUDED
The Leader of the Call to Australia Party, the Reverend Fred Nile, has commended the Prime Minister for refusing to endorse the Sydney gay and lesbian mardi gras.
Mr Nile says it takes a lot of guts for any politician to resist the homosexual lobby in Sydney.
He says no responsible leader should endorse such an obscene parade as the Mardi Gras with what he claims is its message that sodomy is the way to go.
Mr Nile says even the Thomas the Tank Engine float last year was a gigantic penis mounted by ten almost naked males, yet parents took their children along to applaud it.
ANZ STAFF WARN OF ONGOING STRIKE ACTION
ANZ Bank employees are warning of a long-term industrial campaign against plans to restructure the organisation.
The employees today refused to impose anything but government fees and charges.
They're angry about proposals for massive job losses.
Tony Beck from the Finance Sector Union is warning of more action if the bank doesn't listen to employees' concerns.
GUN BUY BACK PROGRAM HAILED A SUCCESS
Federal Attorney-General, Daryl Williams, says more than a quarter of a million firearms will be handed in by the end of the festive season.
The national tally for the guns buy back scheme has reached 238-thousand-308 weapons handed in.
Mr Williams expects more than one hundred million dollars will have been paid to owners by the end of the Christmas season.
He says the early success of the buyback campaign is a credit to gun owners who want to do the right thing by their fellow Australians.
Victoria leads the total with more than 126-thousand guns handed in, followed by South Australia and Tasmania.
CASINO COMPANY SEEKS TO IMPROVE FINANCES
Shareholders in the Brisbane-based Casinos Austria International have agreed to issue more than 25 million shares to its parent company in a move to raise 18 million dollars.
The chief executive of Casinos Austria International, Alex Tucek says it will be used to improve the company's financial position.
The funds would also allow it to extend its existing casino operations and pursue further development opportunities.
Mr Tucek says 12 million dollars of the new capital will be used to reduce the debt on Casino Canberra...from 25 million dollars to 13 million.
He told shareholders the company has experienced a range of teething problems in its first two years as a public company but directors are forecasting a return to profitability in 1997.
12 MILLION TO REDEVELOP CANBERRA STADIUM
The conversion of the ACT's Bruce Stadium into a rectangular football field for soccer matches in the 2000 Olympics is expected to cost Canberra taxpayers around 12 million dollars.
The ACT Government will appoint a project manager immediately to oversee the redevelopment of the stadium, following confirmation Canberra is amongst the five cities to host Olympic soccer matches.
Chief Minister Kate Carnell says the exact Government contribution to the 27 million dollar project will remain secret until the tenderers are appointed.
MORE RADIO STATIONS FOR SYDNEY
Plans are underway to open more radio stations in Sydney.
The Australian Broadcasting Authority has released a discussion paper that indicates Sydney has at least one and possibly up to four FM-frequencies available.
The paper's been forwarded to industry bodies, and existing and potential broadcasters in Sydney for comment.
STRANGE GOINGS ON IN GOLD COAST SKIES
While children will soon be gazing starwards for a glimpse of Santa's sleigh.....some people on Queensland's Gold Coast have already begun seeing some interesting things in the heavens.

The National UFO Hotline has been inundated with calls about strange lights and movements in southern Gold Coast skies. The Hotline's Ross Dowe says there's been numerous calls reporting unidentified flying objects around Burleigh Heads since 2 am this morning.
He says one report in tonight had two women experiencing a close encounter of the third kind...being able to watch a brightly lit rotating disc while driving along a southern Gold Coast road.
